label: Has activity
summary: Whether the travel plan leads to an activity.
details: Vanilla uses it in the travel planner's destination line: when it is true, the activity's name is added below the destination's province name.

label: Has departed
summary: Whether the travelers of the plan have already set out.
details: Vanilla uses it in the travel planner to choose the text: "Next Destination" once the journey has started, "First Destination" before that.

label: Has next destination
summary: Whether the travel plan still has a destination ahead.
details: Vanilla uses it in the travel planner and the activity planner. When it is true they show the parts about the next stop (such as the estimated arrival and the start button); when it is false they show only a plain start button.

label: Has empty path
summary: Going by its name, whether the travel plan has no route yet; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is returning home
summary: Going by its name, whether the travel plan is the trip back home; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Travels with domicile
summary: Whether the journey moves the traveler's domicile (their movable home, such as an adventurer's camp) along with them.
details: Vanilla uses it in the travel planner: when true, a landless adventurer sees a provisions cost; when false, the normal travel cost breakdown is shown instead. The meaning rests on the name and these uses.

label: Remove travel option
summary: Removes a chosen travel option from the travel plan.
details: It takes one argument, the travel option. Vanilla calls it from a small button on each chosen option, shown only while the journey has not started yet.

label: Travel plan itself
summary: The travel plan's data itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to a travel option's cost text and tooltip, which depend on the plan.

label: Access destination
summary: A function on a travel destination that, going by its name, hands back the destination itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Arrival date
summary: The date the travelers arrived at this destination.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the travel planner's list of stops for destinations already reached ("arrived at ...").

label: Days to arrival
summary: Going by its name, the number of days until the travelers reach this destination; the game documents nothing more.
details: It returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it; it uses GetEstimatedArrivalDays instead.

label: Estimated arrival date
summary: The date the travelers are expected to reach this destination.
details: Vanilla never names it after TravelPlanDestination itself, but reaches it through a plan's next destination (GetNextDestination.GetEstimatedArrivalDate) in travel tooltips and in the activity texts that compare it to an activity's start. That route is a hint, so this rests on the name too.

label: Estimated days to arrival
summary: About how many days remain until the travelers reach this destination.
details: It returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it in the travel planner's list of upcoming stops ("arrival in ~N days").

label: Destination number
summary: The position of this destination in the travel plan's list of stops.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Destination N" and passes it to the route edit window, together with a waypoint's number, to say where a detour is added or removed.

label: Destination province
summary: The province this destination lies in.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the list of stops and compares it with the player's capital to label the stop "Your Capital".

label: Waypoints
summary: The waypoints (detours the player added) on the way to this destination.
details: Vanilla lists them in the route edit window and hides that list when it is empty.

label: Has arrived
summary: Going by its name, whether the travelers have already reached this destination; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Destination itself
summary: A function on a travel destination that, going by its name, hands back the destination itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access travel draft
summary: A function on a travel plan draft that, going by its name, hands back the draft itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Draft plan data
summary: The plan data of a travel plan that is still being drafted and has not started.
details: Vanilla uses it to reach the draft's next destination and its estimated arrival date, for example in the activity summary texts that show the travel time and the time before an activity starts.

label: Travel draft itself
summary: A function on a travel plan draft that, going by its name, hands back the draft itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access travel path
summary: A function on a travel path that, going by its name, hands back the path itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Locations ahead
summary: Going by its name, the places on the travel path that are still ahead; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Move progress
summary: Going by its name, how far the travelers have moved along the current step of the path; the game documents nothing more.
details: It returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Next location
summary: Going by its name, the next place on the travel path; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Previous location
summary: Going by its name, the place on the travel path the travelers came from; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Visited locations
summary: Going by its name, the places on the travel path already passed; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Travel path itself
summary: A function on a travel path that, going by its name, hands back the path itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access waypoint
summary: A function on a travel waypoint that, going by its name, hands back the waypoint itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Waypoint number
summary: The position of this waypoint among the detours on the way to its destination.
details: Vanilla passes it, together with the destination's number, to the route edit window to check, remove or add waypoints at that spot.

label: Waypoint province
summary: The province this waypoint lies in.
details: Vanilla uses it in the route edit window to show the province's name and coat of arms ("via ...").

label: Waypoint itself
summary: A function on a travel waypoint that, going by its name, hands back the waypoint itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Travel cost breakdown
summary: The breakdown of what the planned journey costs, shown in the travel planner.
details: Vanilla shows it when the journey does not move a domicile; with a domicile, a provisions cost is shown instead.

label: Access travel planner
summary: A function on the travel planner window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Draft plan data
summary: The plan data of the travel plan being drafted in the travel planner.
details: Vanilla uses it for the travel option buttons while a draft is open (before the journey has started).

label: Can cancel travel
summary: Whether the player may cancel the current travel plan.
details: Vanilla enables the cancel button with it; GetCanCancelTravelPlanTooltip gives the reason.

label: Can close planner
summary: Whether the travel planner window may be closed right now.
details: Vanilla enables the close button with it; GetCanCloseTooltip gives the reason.

label: Cancel travel
summary: Cancels the current travel plan.
details: Vanilla calls it from the travel planner's cancel button, which is only enabled when CanCancelTravelPlan is true.

label: Close planner
summary: Closes the travel planner window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's close button.

label: Close entourage list
summary: Closes the list of characters travelling along (the entourage) in the travel planner.
details: Vanilla calls it from the list's close buttons.

label: Cancel travel tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the cancel travel button, such as why it cannot be used.
details: Vanilla shows it on the cancel button.

label: Close planner tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the travel planner's close button, such as why it cannot be closed.
details: Vanilla shows it on the close button.

label: Cancel button text
summary: The label of the travel planner's cancel travel button.

label: Destination picture
summary: The picture shown behind the destination in the travel planner.
details: Vanilla uses it as a faint background behind the destination text.

label: Entourage list
summary: The list of characters travelling along (the entourage) shown in the travel planner.
details: Vanilla uses it as the content of the entourage list window.

label: Medium danger places
summary: How many places on the route have a medium chance of danger.
details: It returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it next to the counts of low and high danger places.

label: Planner name
summary: A text from the travel planner window that, going by its name, is a name; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the GetName lines given belong to other types.

label: Provisions cost
summary: The provisions the journey costs, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it to a landless adventurer whose domicile travels with them; GetProvisionsCostBreakdown explains it in a tooltip.

label: Provisions cost breakdown
summary: A tooltip text that breaks down the journey's provisions cost.

label: Start button text
summary: The label of the travel planner's button that starts the journey.

label: Travel modifiers
summary: The temporary modifiers that affect the current journey.
details: Vanilla shows them as icons once the journey has started, with a "no modifiers" text when the list is empty.

label: Travel plan
summary: The travel plan shown in the travel planner, when the journey has already started.
details: The window has either a started plan or a draft, never both (a vanilla comment says so); HasTravelPlanDraft tells which. Vanilla checks whether this plan is valid to tell the two apart.

label: Travel plan data
summary: The plan data shown in the travel planner, whether the plan has started or is still a draft.
details: Vanilla uses it for the parts of the window that are the same in both cases.

label: Travel plan draft
summary: The travel plan being drafted in the travel planner, before the journey starts.
details: Only present when there is no started plan; HasTravelPlanDraft tells which one the window has.

label: Low danger places
summary: How many places on the route have a low chance of danger.
details: It returns a whole number.

label: High danger places
summary: How many places on the route have a high chance of danger.
details: It returns a whole number.

label: Has travel draft
summary: Whether the travel planner holds a draft (a journey not yet started) rather than a started plan.
details: Vanilla's comment in the window says to use it to know which of the two is present; it switches the travel option lists with it.

label: Entourage list open
summary: Whether the list of characters travelling along is open.
details: Vanilla shows that list with it in the travel and activity planners.

label: Is linked
summary: Whether the travel planner is linked to something else; going by its uses, the destination is then fixed.
details: Vanilla disables the change destination button while it is true and shows an extra area at the bottom right when it is true and no journey has started. What the planner is linked to (for example an activity) is not documented.

label: Open entourage list
summary: Going by its name, opens the list of characters travelling along; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it opens the list with ToggleEntourageListWindow.

label: Open travel options
summary: Opens the window for choosing travel options for the journey.
details: Vanilla calls it from the travel option buttons of the travel planner.

label: Open route editing
summary: Opens the window for editing the journey's route.
details: Vanilla calls it from the travel planner's edit route button.

label: Travel planner itself
summary: A function on the travel planner window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Start travel
summary: Starts the planned journey.
details: Vanilla calls it from the start buttons of the travel planner; one of them is disabled when the travelers would arrive after the activity begins.

label: Toggle entourage list
summary: Opens the list of characters travelling along, or closes it when it is open.
details: Vanilla calls it from the travel planner's entourage button.

label: Access point of interest type
summary: A function on a point of interest type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Point of interest description
summary: Going by its name, the description of a type of point of interest (a place worth visiting while travelling).
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the GetDescription lines given belong to other types.

label: Point of interest icon
summary: Going by its name, the icon of a type of point of interest.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the GetIcon lines given belong to other types. The game documents no return type.

label: Point of interest name
summary: Going by its name, the display name of a type of point of interest.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the GetName lines given belong to other types.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the display name of a type of point of interest, without the tooltip names usually carry.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines given belong to other types.

label: Has icon
summary: Going by its name, whether a type of point of interest has an icon.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the HasIcon lines given belong to other types. The game documents no return type, though the name suggests yes or no.

label: Point of interest type itself
summary: A function on a point of interest type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access point of interest icon
summary: A function on the points of interest map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon data itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Point of interest description
summary: The description text in the tooltip of a point of interest icon on the map.
details: Points of interest are places worth visiting while travelling.

label: Point of interest icon
summary: The picture of the point of interest shown inside its map pin.
details: Vanilla shows it only while the point has not been visited yet; a visited mark replaces it afterwards.

label: Point of interest province
summary: The province where the point of interest on the map lies.
details: Vanilla uses it and the province's title in the point of interest tooltip.

label: Several points of interest
summary: Whether the province has more than one point of interest.
details: Vanilla then adds a background showing that the map pin stands for several points.

label: Has unvisited point
summary: Whether the province has a point of interest the player has not visited yet.
details: Vanilla shows the point's own icon when true and a visited mark when false.

label: On travel route
summary: Whether the point of interest lies on the planned travel route.
details: Vanilla makes the map pin glow green when true.

label: Click point of interest
summary: What happens when the player left-clicks a point of interest pin on the map.
details: Vanilla calls it from the pin's button; what the click does is not documented.

label: Right-click point of interest
summary: What happens when the player right-clicks a point of interest pin on the map.
details: Vanilla calls it from the pin's button; what the click does is not documented.

label: Point of interest icon itself
summary: A function on the points of interest map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon data itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access travel map icon
summary: A function on a province's travel map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Travel danger
summary: The travel danger of the province, for its icon on the map.
details: Vanilla uses it as data for the danger marker of the travel map icon.

label: Points of interest
summary: The points of interest of the province, for its travel icon on the map.
details: Vanilla uses it as data for the point of interest pin.

label: Has travel danger
summary: Whether the province holds a danger for travelers.
details: Vanilla shows the danger marker on the map with it.

label: Has points of interest
summary: Whether the province has points of interest for travelers.
details: Vanilla shows the point of interest pin on the map with it.

label: Provisions critical
summary: Whether travel provisions would be critically low at this province.
details: Vanilla shows a critical provisions warning on the map with it. Going by the name and that use.

label: Provisions low
summary: Whether travel provisions would be low at this province.
details: Vanilla shows a low provisions warning on the map with it. Going by the name and that use.

label: Is current location
summary: Whether this province is where the player is now.
details: Vanilla shows the player's portrait on the map there.

label: Travel map icon itself
summary: A function on a province's travel map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access route editing
summary: A function on the route edit window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Add detour after departure
summary: Starts adding a waypoint (a detour) right after the place the journey departs from.
details: Vanilla calls it from the plus button next to the departure location, shown when CanAddWaypointAfterDeparture is true; the player then picks a province.

label: Add detour after destination
summary: Starts adding a waypoint (a detour) right after a destination.
details: It takes one argument, the destination's number (TravelPlanDestination.GetIndex).

label: Add detour after waypoint
summary: Starts adding a waypoint (a detour) right after another waypoint.
details: It takes two arguments: the destination's number and the waypoint's number.

label: Add detour before destination
summary: Going by its name, starts adding a waypoint right before a destination; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument, going by the related functions the destination's number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Add detour before waypoint
summary: Going by its name, starts adding a waypoint right before another waypoint; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes two arguments, going by the related functions the destination's and the waypoint's numbers. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Apply route changes
summary: Applies the edited route to the travel plan.
details: Vanilla calls it from the Apply button, which is only enabled when the route is valid, and closes the window right after.

label: Can add after departure
summary: Whether a waypoint can be added right after the departure location.
details: Vanilla shows the plus button with it.

label: Can add after destination
summary: Whether a waypoint can be added right after a given destination.
details: It takes one argument, the destination's number.

label: Can add after waypoint
summary: Whether a waypoint can be added right after a given waypoint.
details: It takes two arguments: the destination's number and the waypoint's number.

label: Can add before destination
summary: Going by its name, whether a waypoint can be added right before a destination; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Can add before waypoint
summary: Going by its name, whether a waypoint can be added right before another waypoint; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes two arguments. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Can remove waypoint
summary: Whether a given waypoint can be removed from the route.
details: It takes two arguments: the destination's number and the waypoint's number. Vanilla shows the remove button with it.

label: Close route editing
summary: Closes the route edit window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the close and Cancel buttons, and after applying the changes.

label: Route problem text
summary: The text that explains why the edited route is not valid.
details: Vanilla shows it as an error text while IsRouteValid is false.

label: Travel plan data
summary: The data of the travel plan whose route is being edited.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data for the whole window.

label: Travel has started
summary: Whether the journey whose route is edited is already under way.
details: Vanilla shows the window's Cancel button only when it is true. Going by the name and that use.

label: Is final destination
summary: Going by its name, whether a given destination is the last one of the route; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument, presumably the destination's number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Quick edit mode
summary: Whether the route edit window is in quick edit mode.
details: The game's instruction texts say holding Shift turns it on; then a left click adds a waypoint and a right click removes one. Vanilla switches the instruction text with it.

label: Route is valid
summary: Whether the edited route can be used.
details: Vanilla enables the Apply button with it and shows an error text (GetRouteValidDesc) when it is false.

label: Is picking province
summary: Going by its name, whether the player is currently picking a province for a waypoint; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Picking province here
summary: Whether the player is picking a province for a new waypoint at a given spot of the route.
details: It takes two arguments: the destination's number and the waypoint's number. Vanilla marks that spot in the list with it.

label: Picking before destination
summary: Whether the player is picking a province for a detour just before a given destination.
details: It takes one argument, the destination's number. Vanilla shows an "add detour here" row with it.

label: Remove waypoint
summary: Removes a waypoint (a detour) from the route.
details: It takes two arguments: the destination's number and the waypoint's number.

label: Route editing itself
summary: A function on the route edit window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Stop picking province
summary: Stops picking a province for a new waypoint, without adding one.
details: Vanilla calls it from the cancel button of the "select a province" bar.

label: Budget law groups
summary: The groups of budget laws listed in the window for changing treasury budgets.
details: Each row is one budget category (vanilla has ministry, salary, military and cardinal budgets).

label: New budget tooltip
summary: The tooltip about a budget category's new total in the budget window.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group.

label: Selected budget law
summary: The law currently selected in a budget category of the budget window.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla shows the law's short name between the decrease and increase buttons.

label: Access budget window
summary: A function on the budget window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Can lower budget
summary: Whether a budget category can be stepped down to a lower law.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla enables the decrease button with it.

label: Can enact budget
summary: Whether the new budget can be enacted.
details: Vanilla enables the Enact Budget button with it; GetCanEnactBudgetDescription explains it in the tooltip.

label: Can raise budget
summary: Whether a budget category can be stepped up to a higher law.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla enables the increase button with it.

label: Close budget window
summary: Closes the window for changing treasury budgets.
details: Vanilla calls it from the close and Cancel buttons.

label: Lower budget
summary: Steps a budget category down to the next lower law in the budget window.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla calls it from the "<" button next to the selected law of a budget category; the button is enabled by CanDecreaseBudgetGroupLaw.

label: Enact budget
summary: Enacts the new treasury budget set up in the window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the Enact Budget button; the cost is shown next to it.

label: Change allocation laws
summary: Going by its name and its button ("Change Allocation Laws"), enacts only the changed budget laws.
details: Vanilla's button for it is hidden (visible = no), so it is not used in the game's interface.

label: Base rate change
summary: Going by its name, how much a budget category's base rate changes; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument and returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Budget capacity change
summary: How much the treasury budget capacity changes with the new budget.
details: Vanilla shows it as "(change: +N)" after the new capacity.

label: Budget category key
summary: The key of a budget category, such as SALARY.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla builds the category's name text from it, and shows the base rate with the gold icon for SALARY and with the treasury icon for the others.

label: Enactment effects
summary: The text listing the effects of enacting the new budget.
details: Vanilla shows it under "Effects of Budget Enactment".

label: Recipient count change
summary: How much the number of characters paid from a budget category changes.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla shows it as the change after the earlier count in a tooltip.

label: Surplus change
summary: How much the unallocated part of the budget changes with the new budget.
details: Vanilla shows it with a plus or minus sign in the summary row of unallocated or deficit funds.

label: Category total change
summary: How much a budget category's total changes with the new budget.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla shows it in the trend column.

label: Total budget change
summary: How much the sum of all budget categories changes with the new budget.
details: Vanilla shows it in the Total row.

label: Enact budget tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the Enact Budget button, such as why it cannot be used.

label: Current allocated share
summary: Going by its name, the share of the budget allocated under the current budget; the game documents nothing more.
details: It returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Current allocation
summary: Going by its name, a budget category's allocation under the current budget; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument and returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Current base rate
summary: Going by its name, a budget category's base rate under the current budget; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument and returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Current base rate count
summary: A budget window function about a category's current base rate; going by its name, a count tied to it. The game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument and returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Previous budget capacity
summary: The treasury budget capacity of the budget now in force.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Previous budget capacity", with the date that budget was enacted.

label: Last enactment date
summary: The date the current budget was enacted.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Last budget enacted" and next to the previous capacity.

label: Previous recipient count
summary: How many recipients a budget category had at the start of the current budget's enactment.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla shows it in a tooltip, followed by the change.

label: Current surplus
summary: Going by its name, the unallocated part of the current budget; the game documents nothing more.
details: It returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Current category total
summary: Going by its name, a budget category's total under the current budget; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument and returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Current budget total
summary: Going by its name, the sum of all categories under the current budget; the game documents nothing more.
details: It returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: New allocated share
summary: The share of the budget the new budget allocates, as a fraction of 1.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage in the Total row and shows 1 minus it as the unallocated share.

label: New allocation
summary: Going by its name, a budget category's allocation under the new budget; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument and returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: New base rate
summary: A budget category's base rate under the new budget.
details: It takes one argument, the budget law group. Vanilla shows it in the base rate column, in gold for the salary budget and in treasury for the others.
